candidate.purpose: single unlimited-time feasibility probe on a third streaming engine, after Edge0 (no tool-calling support at all) and Hebrus (HTTP 500 crash on a KV-cache-miss token-mismatch mid-conversation) both failed on infrastructure before reaching the repair task

default.context_label: 16384-token context, forced 16-slot expert cache profile (MFERENCE_EXPERT_SLOTS=16 env var, not a CLI flag)

slot_cache_clear.explanation: Mference exposes no llama.cpp-style slot erase endpoint; prompt cache mode is single-prefix and is per-conversation, not per-attempt.

policy.backend_note: This is a feasibility probe, not a screen, same discipline as HEBRUS-QWEN36-FEASIBILITY-IMMER: no 300s budget, single seed, because prior scored attempts on every other engine truncated or crashed before finishing. Server is started externally (--external-server) rather than managed by the runner, because MferenceServer's request schema needed a local patch to accept go-agent's parallel_tool_calls=false (see benchmarks/optimization/mference-parallel-tool-calls.patch, applied to source commit 1eda4b3bbf654038630d13dc9a41bb80e78496a8 at github.com/joaoin0x/Mference); MferenceServer itself has no --version/--build-info output, so serverBinaryInfo's mference branch only checks the process starts (exit 0), and provenance is this commit hash plus the patch file. presence_penalty is not implemented by Mference at all (silently has no effect; Qwen's own recommended non-thinking value of 1.5 cannot be honored here) -- a known, accepted quality gap, not a bug to chase. MFERENCE_EXPERT_SLOTS=16 was set at server start to force the conservative ~1.45 GB slot profile; left on auto-detect, this exactly-16-GiB host would select the 32-slot profile based on total physical RAM, not the live ~3 GiB reclaimable memory actually measured. max_server_footprint_bytes matches the same 2026-09-17 measured live ceiling used for the Hebrus probe.

experiments.hypothesis: Mference's default prompt-cache reuse (single-prefix) and fixed-size linear-attention state (no growing KV cache) let it complete a full agentic repair within the hour where Hebrus crashed on the second turn and Edge0 could not be tried at all.
